title: Brij Mohan v. State of U.P. — s.135 FIR not quashed; arrest safeguards and compounding
coram: V.K. Shukla, J. and Shashi Kant, J.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 13301 of 2014
disposition: s.135 FIR not quashed; CrPC arrest safeguards directed; compounding available
headnote: Division Bench refused to quash an FIR under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003, because it disclosed a cognizable offence. Arrest, if at all, of a person whose offence cannot attract more than seven years' imprisonment must comply with Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A Cr.P.C. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Brij Mohan filed a criminal miscellaneous writ petition to quash FIR dated 8 February 2014, Case Crime No. 67 of 2014, registered at P.S. Daurala, District Meerut, under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003. Arrest had not been made. He argued that the FIR should be quashed; that a proved charge could not attract more than seven years' imprisonment, so arrest should not be mechanical; and that the offence was compoundable. The complainant and the State were represented.

holding_units.topic: s.135 FIR — quash refused; arrest and compounding
holding_units.holding: An FIR under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence is not liable to be quashed. Where arrest has not been made and the offence cannot attract a sentence exceeding seven years, police must, if arrest is to be effectuated, comply with Section 41(1)(b) read with Section 41-A Cr.P.C.; breach may be complained of before the Magistrate. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: Quash of a s.135 FIR refused as it disclosed a cognizable offence; arrest, if at all, tied to CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A because sentence cannot exceed seven years; compounding left to the Supply Code, 2005.
